questions.q: The number of solutions of equation, $sin5xcos3x = sin6xcos2x$,~in the interval  \left[0, \pi\right]$ are$
questions.solution:
Given,

$sin5xcos3x = sin6xcos2x$

The given equation can be written as

$2sin5xcos3x = 2sin6xcos2x$

$⇒ sin8x + sin2x = sin8x + sin4x; \left[∵ 2sinAcosB = sin \left($A + B\right) + $sin\left($A - B\right)\right]$

~$⇒ sin2x - sin4x = 0$

$⇒ - 2sinxcos3x = 0,$

Hence,~$sinx = 0$~or $cos3x = 0 .$

$x = $n\pi \left($n \in I\right)$~or~$3x = k$\pi + $\dfrac{π}{2} \left($k \in I\right)$

Therefore, since $x \in \left[0, \pi\right],$the given equation is satisfied,~$x = 0, \pi, \dfrac{π}{6}, \dfrac{π}{2}$~or~$\dfrac{5\pi}{6}.$Hence number of solutions are~$5.

$

Then, $\cos x=\frac{2 \cos (x-y) \cos (x+y)}{\cos (x+y)+\cos (x-y)}\cos x=\frac{\cos 2 x+\cos 2 y}{2 \cos x \cdot \cos y}\cos x=\frac{2 \cos ^2 x+2 \cos ^2 y-2}{2 \cos x \cdot \cos y}\cos ^2 x \cdot \cos y=\cos ^2 x+\cos ^2 y-1\cos ^2 x(\cos y-1)=\left(\cos ^2 y-1\right)\cos ^2 x(1-\cos y)=\left(1-\cos ^2 y\right)\cos ^2 x\left(2 \sin ^2 \frac{y}{2}\right)=\sin ^2 y\cos ^2 x\left(2 \sin ^2 \frac{y}{2}\right)=\left(2 \sin \frac{y}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{y}{2}\right)^2\cos ^2 x\left(2 \sin ^2 \frac{y}{2}\right)=4 \sin ^2 \frac{y}{2} \cdot \cos ^2 \frac{y}{2}\cos ^2 x=\left(2 \cos ^2 \frac{y}{2}-1\right)+1\cos y+1=\cos ^2 x$

& \Rightarrow \tan $\theta+\frac{\tan \theta+\sqrt{3}}{1-\sqrt{3} \tan \theta}+\frac{\tan \theta-\sqrt{3}}{1+\sqrt{3} \tan \theta}=$3 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \tan $\theta+\frac{8 \tan \theta}{1-3 \tan ^2 \theta}=$3 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{9 \tan \theta-3 \tan ^3 \theta}{1-3 \tan ^2 \theta}=$3 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3 \tan 3 $\theta=$3 \Rightarrow \tan 3 $\theta=$1 \\
&
\end{aligned} Hence, option (2) is correct.

questions.q: What is the minimum value of $\cos \theta+\cos 2 \theta$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{A}=\cos \theta+\cos 2 \theta\therefore$ On differentiating w.r.t. to $\theta$, we get
$\frac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{d} \theta}=-\sin \theta-2 \sin 2 \theta$
Put $\frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{d} \theta}=0$ for maximaor minima. $\sin \theta+2 \sin 2 \theta=0 \Rightarrow \sin \theta+4 \sin \theta \cos \theta\Rightarrow \sin \theta(1+4 \cos \theta)=0\Rightarrow \sin \theta=0$, or $4 \cos \theta+1=0\Rightarrow \cos \theta=1$ or $\cos \theta=-\frac{1}{4}$
Now, $\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d} \theta^{2}}=-\cos \theta-4 \cos 2 \theta=-\cos \theta-4  \left(2 \cos ^{2} \theta-1\right)$
For $\cos \$bar{\ttheta}=1\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{~A$A}}{\mathrm{~d} $\theta^{2}}=-\cos \t$theta-4\left($2 \cos ^{2} $\theta-$1\right)=-1-4(2(1)-1)=-1-4=-5 < 0$
So, A is maximum at $\cos $\theta=$1\Rightarrow\$left(\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d} \theta^{2}}\right)_{\cos \theta=\frac{-1}{4}}=\ffrac{1}{4}-$4\left($2 $\cdot $\frac{1}{16}-1\right)>0\quad\left[\right.$Since \left.\cos2 \theta=2 \cos ^{2} \theta-1\right]\therefore \mathrm{A}$is minimum at $\theta=\cos ^{-1} $\$left(\frac{-1}{4}\right)
Now minimum value of $\cos \theta+\cos 2 \theta$
or of $\cos \theta+2 \cos ^{2} \theta-1=\$left(\frac{-1}{4}\right)+$2\$left(\frac{1}{16}\r$right)-1=\frac{-1}{4}+\f$frac{1}{8}-1=\frac{-2+1-8}{8}=\frac{-9}{8}$

questions.q: The number of $x \in \left[$0, 2$\pi\right] for which \left|\sqrt{2\sin^{4}x + 18\cos^{2}x} - \sqrt{2\cos^{4}x + 18\sin^{2}x}\right| =$1$ is:$
questions.solution:
Given

\left|\sqrt{2\sin^{4} ⁡ x + 18\cos^{2} ⁡ x} - \sqrt{2\cos^{4} ⁡ x + 18\sin^{2} ⁡ x}\right| = 1$

$⇒ \sqrt{2\sin^{4} ⁡ x + 18\cos^{2} ⁡ x} - \sqrt{2\cos^{4} ⁡ x + 18\sin^{2} ⁡ x} = \pm 1$

$⇒ \sqrt{2\sin^{4} ⁡ x + 18\cos^{2} ⁡ x} = \pm 1 + \sqrt{2\cos^{4} ⁡ x + 18\sin^{2} ⁡ x}$

By squaring both the sides, we get

$2\sin^{4} ⁡ x + 18\cos^{2} ⁡ x = 1 + 2\cos^{4} ⁡ x + 18\sin^{2} ⁡ x \pm 2\sqrt{2\cos^{4} ⁡ x + 18\sin^{2} ⁡ x}$

$⇒ 2\left(\sin^{4} ⁡ x - \cos^{4} ⁡ x\right) + 18\left(\cos^{2} ⁡ x - \sin^{2} ⁡ x\right) = 1 \pm 2\sqrt{2\cos^{4} ⁡ x + 18\sin^{2} ⁡ x}$

$⇒ 2\left(\sin^{2} ⁡ x - \cos^{2} ⁡ x\right) + 18\left(\cos^{2} ⁡ x - \sin^{2} ⁡ x\right) = 1 \pm 2\sqrt{2\cos^{4} ⁡ x + 18\sin^{2} ⁡ x}$

$⇒ 16\left(\cos^{2} ⁡ x - \sin^{2} ⁡ x\right) = 1 \pm 2\sqrt{2\cos^{4} ⁡ x + 18\sin^{2} ⁡ x}$

$⇒ 16cos ⁡ 2x - 1 = \pm 2\sqrt{2{\left(\dfrac{1 + cos ⁡ 2x}{2}\right)}^{2} + 9\left(1 - cos ⁡ 2x\right)}$

Squaring both sides again, we get

$256\cos^{2} ⁡ 2x + 1 - 32cos ⁡ 2x = 4 \left(\dfrac{1 + 2cos ⁡ 2x + \cos^{2} ⁡ 2x}{2} ++9 \left($1 - cos ⁡ 2x\right)\right)$

$256\cos^{2} ⁡ 2x + 1 - $32\text\cos$⁡ 2x = 2 \left($19 - 16cos ⁡ 2x + \cos^{2} ⁡ 2x\right)$

$⇒ 254\cos^{2} ⁡ 2x = 37 ⇒ \cos^{2} ⁡ 2x = \dfrac{37}{254}⇒ cos ⁡ 2x = $\pm $\sqrt{\dfrac{37}{254}} \in \left[-$1, 1\right]$
Since, the solutions lie in all four quadrants, there are $8$ solutions which satisfy the equation.

$

We need to find the value of

$36 \left(4\cos^{2}{9}^{∘} - 1\right) \left($4\cos^{2}{27}^{∘} - 1\$right)\left($4\cos^{2}{81}^{∘} - 1\$right)\left(4\cos^{2}{243}^{∘} - 1\right)$

$= 36 \left[ \left($4\sin^{2}{18}^{∘} - 4 + 1\right)\left(4\sin^{2}{54}^{∘} - 4 + 1\right)\right]$

$= 36 \left[ \left($4\sin^{2}{18}^{∘} - 3\right)\left($4\sin^{2}{54}^{∘} - 3\right)\right]$
$= 36\left[\left$\{\dfrac{ \left(\sqrt{5} -$1\right)2}{4} -$3\right\} \left$\{\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{5} + 1\right)2}{4} -$3\right\}$\right]$
$= 36 \left[ \left\{ \left($6 - 2\sqrt{5} -12\$right)4\left($6 + $2\sqrt{5} -$12\right)4\right\}\right]$
$= - $36\left[\left$\{\dfrac{\left(2\sqrt{5}\right)2 - 36}{16}\right\}\right] =36$

Given, $tanA = \dfrac{1}{x\left(x^{2} + x + 1\right)}, tanB = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} + x + 1}$ and $tanC = \left(x^{- 3} + x^{- 2} + x^{- 1}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1 + x + x^{2}}{x\sqrt{x}}$

$⇒ tan\left(A + B\right) = \dfrac{x^{2} + x + 1}{x\sqrt{x}}$

$⇒ tan\left(A + B\right) = tanC$

$⇒ A + B = C$
